title: Blacklist a kernel module to prevent loading
summary: Blacklisting prevents a kernel module from loading automatically at boot. This is useful if a driver causes conflicts or you do not need the hardware.

steps.explain: Create a file like /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist.conf and add the line: blacklist <MODULE_NAME>

rollback.explain: Delete the file /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist.conf or remove the blacklist line.

warnings: Blacklisting only prevents automatic loading. The module can still be loaded manually or by dependencies.
If the module is in the initramfs, you may need to regenerate it.
